results.name: Cable Fly Machine Mid
instructions: Set both pulleys at chest height and stand in the middle holding a handle in each hand.
Step forward with a slight bend in your elbows and your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Return slowly to the stretched position and repeat.
tips: Keep the elbow angle fixed throughout.
Squeeze your chest when the handles meet.
results.description: Cable Fly Machine Mid is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Low Fly
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at a low position. Grasp the handles with your palms facing forward and arms extended down out to your sides. Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly staggered for stability.
Stand upright with your back straight. Bring the handles together in front of your body in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and palms should face upwards.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Cable Low Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Cable Lying Fly
instructions: Lie on a flat bench between a dual crossover machine and your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with your palms facing up and arms extended to the sides at chest level.
Raise the handles over your chest in a wide arc motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Return to the starting position by lowering the handles out to your sides in a wide arc motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you build strength.
Make sure the bench is stable and positioned securely between the cable machines.
results.description: Cable Lying Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.

results.description: Cable Machine High to Low is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Cable Machine Low to High
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at a low position. Grasp the handles with your palms facing upward and arms extended at your sides. Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly staggered for stability.
Stand upright with your back straight. Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and palms should face upwards.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders as you lift the handles.
results.description: Cable Machine Low to High is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Cable Middle Fly
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable fly machine with the pulleys set at mid-chest height, with one foot in front of the other and knees slightly bent. Hold the handles with both hands, arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Keep your back straight and maintain a slight bend at the hips and knees for stability.
Pull the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping your arms slightly bent, until your hands meet in the centerline of your chest.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to reduce strain on your joints.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Cable Middle Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Cable One Arm Chest Fly Bent
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable fly machine with the pulleys set at mid-chest height, with feet just wider than shoulder-width and bend at the hips and knees and lean towards the floor. Place your left hand to your knee for support.

Hold the handle with your right hand, arm extended out to the side at shoulder height, palm facing forward. Bring the handle opposite your chest in a wide arc motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position, maintaining control and the bend in your elbow.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to reduce strain on your joints.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you build strength.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
results.description: Cable One Arm Chest Fly Bent is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Standing Up Straight Crossovers
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable crossover machine with the pulleys set at the highest point. Grasp the handles with each hand, palms facing forward.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart with one foot forward and the other back and knees slightly bent. Keep your back straight and arms extended out to your sides.
Pull the handles down and forward until they meet in front of your hips. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles down and in front of your chest and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles during the movement.
results.description: Cable Standing Up Straight Crossovers is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Cable Upper Chest Crossover
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable crossover machine with the pulleys set at the lowest point. Grasp the handles with each hand, palms facing forward.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Pull the handles up and forward until they meet over your chest.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles down and in front of your chest and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles during the movement.
results.description: Cable Upper Chest Crossover is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Chest Bench Press Correct Stance
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor, positioned so that your eyes are directly under the barbell. Grip the barbell with a slightly wider than shoulder-width grip, palms facing away from you, ensuring your hands are evenly spaced on the bar.
Place your feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Engage your legs and glutes, pushing your feet into the floor to create a strong foundation.
Maintain a natural arch in your lower back, keeping your shoulders and glutes in contact with the bench. Retract your shoulder blades and tuck them firmly into the bench for stability.
tips: Engage your core muscles throughout the exercise to maintain stability and protect your lower back.
Ensure your feet are firmly planted on the floor to provide stability and prevent your lower back from arching excessively.
Ensure your head remains in contact with the bench, and avoid lifting it during the press.
results.description: Chest Bench Press Correct Stance is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.
